en.For some barbarians, rage is a means to: For some firefighters, adrenaline is a means to an end, and that end is getting through the door no matter what is on the other side. Smoke Eaters are the ones who go in first and come out last, soot-black and grinning. When the Adrenaline hits, you thrill in the chaos, heedless of your own health or well-being.
en.Barbarians of the Spirit Beast are claim: Wildland crews spend whole seasons on the fire line: cutting breaks, hauling hose up ridges, sleeping in the dirt. Every member settles into a role, and the role becomes who they are. When the Adrenaline hits, the crew's training takes over: the ram who smashes through, the siren who screams the warning, the anchor who never gives ground, the hook who drags people out.
en.In battle, you fight with primal ferocit:
In a fight, you go on pure adrenaline. On your turn, you can get your Adrenaline up as a bonus action. While your Adrenaline is up, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor:
- You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
- When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll. This bonus increases as you level.
- You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
If you can use techniques, you can't use them or concentrate on them while your Adrenaline is up.
Your Adrenaline lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end it on your turn as a bonus action.
Once you have used Adrenaline the maximum number of times for your Firefighter level, you must finish a long rest before you can use it again. You can use it 2 times at 1st level, 3 at 3rd, 4 at 6th, 5 at 12th, and 6 at 17th.
en.While you are not wearing any armor, you: Years of hauling hose, gear and people have made you hard to hurt. While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can throw asi: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense and wade in swinging. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.
en.At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense: At 2nd level, you have a trained feel for when a structure, a room or a crowd isn't as it should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps, collapses and techniques. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.
en.At 3rd level, you choose a path that sha: At 3rd level, you choose the Crew you trained with, which shapes how your Adrenaline works. Choose Smoke Eater or Wildland Crew. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.
en.Starting when you choose this path at 3r: Starting when you choose this Crew at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when your Adrenaline comes up. If you do so, for as long as your Adrenaline lasts you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your Adrenaline ends, the crash hits and you suffer one level of exhaustion.
en.Starting at 5th level, your speed increa: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing heavy armor.
en.Beginning at 6th level, you can't be cha: Beginning at 6th level, nobody can talk you into anything or scare you off while your Adrenaline is up: you can't be charmed or frightened. If you are charmed or frightened when your Adrenaline comes up, the effect is suspended for as long as it lasts.
en.By 7th level, your instincts are so hone:
By 7th level, years of answering the alarm have honed your reflexes so that you have advantage on initiative rolls.
Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren't incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you get your Adrenaline up before doing anything else on that turn.
en.Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.
en.Beginning at 10th level, you can use you:
Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
 If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.
en.Starting at 11th level, your rage can ke:
Starting at 11th level, your Adrenaline can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while your Adrenaline is up and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.
Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.
en.Starting at 14th level, when you take da: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.
en.Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so: Beginning at 15th level, your Adrenaline burns so hot that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.
en.Beginning at 18th level, if your total f: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.
en.At 20th level, you embody the power of t: At 20th level, you are at the absolute peak of human conditioning. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.
en.While raging: +10 ft speed; charge 20 ft: While on Adrenaline: +10 ft speed; charge 20 ft straight and hit in melee → Strength save or knocked prone.
en.While raging: bonus action cry, one crea: While on Adrenaline: bonus action bellow, one creature within 30 ft makes a Wisdom save or is frightened of you until the end of its next turn.
en.While raging: +1 AC, and you can't be pu: While on Adrenaline: +1 AC, and you can't be pushed, pulled or knocked prone against your will.
en.While raging: after a melee hit, grapple: While on Adrenaline: after a melee hit, grapple as a bonus action with advantage; whoever you grapple has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you.
en.Choose a spirit beast: Stag, Raven, Tort: Choose a crew role: Ram, Siren, Anchor, or Hook. Your choice determines the benefit of this feature and of your later role features; you can change your role when you gain a Firefighter level. While your Adrenaline is up you gain: • Ram: your speed increases by 10 feet, and if you move at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and hit it with a melee attack on the same turn, it must succeed on a Strength save (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be knocked prone. • Siren: as a bonus action, you let out a harsh, wailing bellow; one creature of your choice within 30 feet that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom save (same DC as the Ram) or be frightened of you until the end of its next turn. • Anchor: you gain +1 AC and can't be pushed, pulled, or knocked prone against your will. • Hook: when you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can try to grapple it as a bonus action, with advantage on the check; a creature you grapple has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you.
en.The spirit beast teaches you the speech: Pulling dogs out of burning barns and horses out of floodwater taught you how animals think. You can read and calm an animal well enough to trade simple ideas with it, as the speak with animals technique, without spending a technique slot, but only by taking 10 extra minutes. In addition, you have advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks, and ordinary animals (never the dead) are indifferent to you unless provoked or trained and driven to attack.
en.You gain a lasting benefit from your spi: Your crew role becomes second nature, active whether or not your Adrenaline is up: • Ram: your long and high jump distances double, and ordinary difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. • Siren: you add your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1) to initiative rolls, allies within 10 feet of you can't be surprised while you aren't, and you can mimic any sound or voice you have heard (a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) reveals the trick). • Anchor: trained breathing and a rag over your face let you work through smoke, gas or water for 1 hour on next to no air, and you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned and against exhaustion. • Hook: with a pike pole, rope and nerve, you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, and advantage on saving throws against poison.
en.Once per rage, as a bonus action, you le: Once each time your Adrenaline comes up, as a bonus action, you bellow the crew's call. Each ally of your choice within 30 feet that can hear you gains temporary hit points equal to your Constitution modifier + half your Firefighter level (rounded down), and has advantage on its next saving throw against being frightened or charmed before the end of its next turn.
en.Your spirit beast's power peaks while yo: Your crew role peaks while your Adrenaline is up: • Ram: when you knock a creature prone with your Ram charge, you can make one melee weapon attack against it as part of the same action (no bonus action needed). • Siren: when an ally you can see within 30 feet is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to burst through the chaos to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the attacker, then make one melee weapon attack against it. • Anchor: once each time your Adrenaline comes up, when you take damage, you can use your reaction to reduce it by an amount equal to your Firefighter level + your Constitution modifier. • Hook: at the start of each of your turns, one creature grappled by you takes bludgeoning damage equal to 1d8 + your Strength modifier, and creatures grappled by you are also restrained.
en.Bards of the College of Lore know someth: Talk Radio hosts know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge from sources as different as library books and callers' gossip. Whether running the morning call-in show or reading the evening news, they know how to keep a whole town glued to the dial. When the show ends, listeners might find themselves questioning everything they held to be true, from the sermons at the local church to their trust in the mayor. A Talk Radio host's loyalty lies in the pursuit of the truth and a good story, not in deference to whoever holds power or preaches from a pulpit. A council member who invites such a host into the room knows that the host would rather be honest than polite. Hosts swap stories over coffee at the station, in diners and in the back of the public library, and they turn up at town meetings and fairs, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.
en.Battle-singers of this college march at: Rock Station hosts lead from the front with a bullhorn or a battered portable amp, keeping time for everyone behind them with drumbeats, riffs and their own hoarse voice. They learned their craft at county fairs, bar gigs and riot-loud concerts, where a song that steadies a terrified crowd is worth more than any polished ballad. To them, every fight has a rhythm, and whoever controls the rhythm controls the street.
en.You have learned to untangle and reshape: You know how to move people with nothing but your voice, your timing and a few props. Your techniques are part of a vast repertoire, tricks you can tune to any situation.
en.You can inspire others through stirring:
You can fire others up with stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Pep Talk die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Pep Talk die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Pep Talk die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Pep Talk die at a time.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest. 
Your Pep Talk die changes when you reach certain levels in this profession. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can add half: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.
en.Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soot:
Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or a good story to help revive your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear you regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points. 
The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this profession: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.
en.At 3rd level, you delve into the advance: At 3rd level, you settle into the Format of your choice, such as Talk Radio. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th and 14th level.
en.When you join the College of Lore at 3rd: When you choose Talk Radio at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
en.Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use:
Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.
When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Pep Talk, rolling a Pep Talk die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll.
You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed (the dead never listen).
en.At 3rd level, choose two of your skill p: At 3rd level, choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. At 10th level, you can choose another two skill proficiencies to gain this benefit.
en.Beginning when you reach 5th level, you: Beginning when you reach 5th level, you regain all of your expended uses of Pep Talk when you finish a short or long rest.
en.At 6th level, you gain the ability to us: At 6th level, you can use a calm, steady voice or a familiar tune to cut through panic and manipulation. As an action, you can start a performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. During that time, you and any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit. The performance ends early if you are incapacitated or silenced or if you voluntarily end it (no action required).
en.At 6th level, you learn two spells of yo: At 6th level, you learn two techniques of your choice from any profession. A technique you choose must be of a level you can use, as shown on the Radio Host table, or a knack. The chosen techniques count as Radio Host techniques for you but don't count against the number of Radio Host techniques you know.
en.By 10th level, you have plundered magica:
By 10th level, you have picked up know-how from every guest, caller and expert who ever sat in your studio. Choose two techniques from any profession, including this one. A technique you choose must be of a level you can use, as shown on the Radio Host table, or a knack. 
The chosen techniques count as Radio Host techniques for you and are included in the number in the Techniques Known column of the Radio Host table. 
You learn two additional techniques from any profession at 14th level and again at 18th level.
en.Starting at 14th level, when you make an: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Pep Talk. Roll a Pep Talk die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the GM tells you whether you succeed or fail.
en.At 20th level, when you roll initiative: At 20th level, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Pep Talk left, you regain one use.
en.When you join the College of Battle Hymn: When you choose Rock Station at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons. You can also use a melee weapon you are proficient with as the tool for your Radio Host techniques, and you can make the gestures your techniques need while holding a weapon or shield in one or both hands.
en.Also at 3rd level, you can lead a marchi:
Also at 3rd level, you can lead a pounding chant in the thick of combat, backed by your bullhorn or amp. As a bonus action, you expend one use of Pep Talk and start the riff. It lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you are incapacitated, if you fall silent (for example, gagged or with your mouth covered), or if you end it (no action required). While the riff lasts:
• Downbeat. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, roll your Pep Talk die and deal extra thunder damage (a point-blank blast of sound) equal to the roll.
• Heads Up. When you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you that can hear you is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to shout a warning that turns the blow, reducing the damage taken by one roll of your Pep Talk die + your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). The first Heads Up during a riff is free; each later one during the same riff expends one use of Pep Talk.
en.Starting at 6th level, you can attack tw: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. In addition, while your Battle Riff is active, the first time on each of your turns that you hit two different creatures with weapon attacks, one friendly creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that can hear you gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + half your Radio Host level (rounded down). These temporary hit points last until the riff ends.
en.At 14th level, your war-song can turn th: At 14th level, your song can turn the tide of a battle. As an action, you start a rousing anthem everyone knows the words to, lasting 1 minute (it ends early if you are incapacitated or silenced). When you start it, you and each friendly creature of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear you gain temporary hit points equal to your Radio Host level, and any of those creatures that are frightened or charmed are no longer so. For the duration, those creatures have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed, and once on each of their turns when one of them hits with a weapon attack, it deals an extra 1d8 thunder damage, swinging to the beat. You also start or refresh your Battle Riff without expending Pep Talk. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
en.Also at 14th level, when you hit a creat: Also at 14th level, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one use of Pep Talk to end the strike with a shriek of amp feedback right in its ear. The target takes extra thunder damage equal to two rolls of your Pep Talk die and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your technique save DC or be deafened and unable to take reactions until the start of your next turn. You can use this feature only once per turn.
en.The Life domain focuses on the vibrant p: The ER runs on one rule: keep them breathing. You worked the doors where the ambulances came in, and you learned to stop bleeding, restart lungs and make hard calls in seconds. When the dead started walking in, you were already used to chaos. Now you carry the ER with you: a trauma bag, a steady voice and a refusal to let anyone else die on your watch while you push the dead back.
en.Gods of lore, memory and discovery hold: You counted pills, caught dosing errors and knew what every drug in the cabinet does to a body, for better or worse. Out here that knowledge is worth more than ammunition. You read people the way you read a chart, and in a fight you spot exactly where someone is weak and tell your friends where to hit.
en.Deities of the sun, the hearth-fire and: You spent your shifts with fire's aftermath: scorched skin, smoke-filled lungs, the long work of healing. You respect flame because you know what it does, and now you use it. Flares, burning fuel and a blinding light in the dark are your tools, and wherever you go, nothing stays hidden for long.
en.Gods of the deep forest, the turning sea: You were the only nurse for miles of farmland in every direction, treating tractor injuries, snakebites and whatever walked in the door. You know which plants heal and which ones kill, and the land is as much your pharmacy as any cabinet. You get along with farmers and hunters, and the woods have always been on your side.
en.Sky-gods, sea-gods and lords of thunder: Hearts stop, and you start them again. You worked the cardiac floor with the crash cart always within reach, and you know exactly how much current a body can take. Now you carry a jury-rigged defibrillator and batteries scavenged from cars. A shock from your paddles leaves the living stunned and the dead jerking on the floor.
en.Gods of thieves, jesters and clever esca: You worked the locked ward, where talking someone down mattered more than any needle. You learned every trick patients used to slip their restraints, and a few of your own. You win by wit rather than force: a misdirection, a borrowed uniform, a calm voice that gets people to do exactly what you need.
en.Gods of battle, conquest and the shield-: Before the hospital, you served as a combat medic. You know how to patch a wound under fire, then pick up a rifle and hold the line. You are part nurse, part squad leader, binding wounds between pushes and calling your team to hit together. Your care is drilled, disciplined and loud.
en.As a conduit for divine power, you can c: Years of medical training let you treat, sedate and stabilize with whatever supplies you can find. You can use Nurse techniques.
en.Choose one domain related to your deity,:
Choose the Ward where you trained: ER, Pharmacy, Burn Unit, Rural Clinic, Cardiology, Psych Ward or Combat Medic. ER is the core Ward; the others are described in their own entries.
Your Ward grants you Ward techniques and other features when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional ways to use Triage when you gain that feature at 2nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 8th, and 17th levels.
en.Each domain has a list of spells--its do:
Each Ward has a list of techniques (its Ward techniques) that you gain at the Nurse levels noted in the Ward description. Once you gain a Ward technique, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of techniques you can prepare each day.
If you have a Ward technique that doesn't appear on the Nurse technique list, the technique is nonetheless a Nurse technique for you.
en.When you choose this domain at 1st level: When you choose this Ward at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor: riot gear, heavy plate carriers and the like.
en.Also starting at 1st level, your healing: Also starting at 1st level, your healing techniques are more effective. Whenever you use a technique of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the technique's level.
en.At 2nd level, you gain the ability to ch:
At 2nd level, you learn to push your training and your gear past their limits when everything goes wrong at once. You start with two such effects: Road Flare and an effect determined by your Ward. Some Wards grant you additional effects as you advance in levels, as noted in the Ward description.
When you use your Triage, you choose which effect to create. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Triage again.
Some Triage effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this profession, the DC equals your Nurse technique save DC.
Beginning at 6th level, you can use your Triage twice between rests, and beginning at 18th level, you can use it three times between rests. When you finish a short or long rest, you regain your expended uses.
en.As an action, you present your holy symb:
As an action, you strike a road flare, hold it high and shout the dead back. Each of the dead (zombies) that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is driven back for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.
A driven-back creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can use your:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Triage to treat the badly injured.
As an action, you work a mass-casualty scene at speed, sorting, packing and dressing wounds, restoring a number of hit points equal to five times your Nurse level.
Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on one of the dead or on a construct.
en.Starting at 5th level, when an undead fa: Starting at 5th level, when one of the dead fails its saving throw against your Road Flare, the creature catches fire and is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold.
en.Beginning at 6th level, you can use your: Beginning at 6th level, you can use your Triage twice between rests, and beginning at 18th level, you can use it three times between rests. When you finish a short or long rest, you regain your expended uses.
en.Beginning at 6th level, the healing spel: Beginning at 6th level, saving someone else keeps you going too. When you use a technique of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the technique's level.
en.At 8th level, you gain the ability to in: At 8th level, you know exactly where a body breaks: arteries, joints, nerves. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 damage of the weapon's type to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
en.Beginning at 10th level, you can call on:
Beginning at 10th level, you can call a Code Blue when your need is great: every radio channel, every contact, every favor anyone ever owed you.
Calling for help requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your Nurse level, help comes through. The GM chooses what form the help takes (survivors arriving, a cache turning up, a lucky break); the effect of any Nurse technique or Ward technique would be appropriate.
If help comes through, you can't use this feature again for 7 days. Otherwise, you can use it again after you finish a long rest.
At 20th level, your Code Blue succeeds automatically, no roll required.
en.Starting at 17th level, when you would n: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a technique, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.
en.At 20th level, your call for interventio: At 20th level, your Code Blue succeeds automatically, no roll required.
en.When you choose this domain at 1st level: When you choose this Ward at 1st level, you learn one additional language of your choice and gain proficiency in two skills chosen from Medicine, History, Investigation, Nature and Religion. You also gain proficiency with your choice of calligrapher's supplies or cartographer's tools.
en.Starting at 1st level, you can whisper a: Starting at 1st level, you can call out a timely fact to a companion. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you (including yourself) makes an ability check, you can use your reaction to add your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1) to the roll. You decide after seeing the d20 roll but before the DM says whether the check succeeds. The creature must be able to hear you.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one: Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one use of your Triage to size up a creature at a glance and say aloud what's wrong with it. As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. You learn its creature type, its damage vulnerabilities, resistances and immunities, its condition immunities, and which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus. In addition, the target has disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against one of your Nurse techniques before the end of your next turn.
en.Beginning at 6th level, a lifetime of st: Beginning at 6th level, years of night shifts and hard cases have steadied your thoughts. You have resistance to psychic damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against illusion techniques and against any effect that would read your thoughts. In addition, you can use detect thoughts without expending a technique slot. Once you use it this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
en.At 8th level, you strike where your know: At 8th level, you strike where you know it will hurt most. Once on each of your turns when you deal damage to a creature with a weapon attack or a Nurse knack, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage of the same type to it. If you targeted that creature with Triage: Diagnosis within the last minute, the extra damage is 2d6 instead. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d6 (3d6 against a creature you have diagnosed).
en.At 17th level, you can understand any sp: At 17th level, years of patient charts, drug inserts and translated discharge papers let you understand any spoken or written language. In addition, as an action you can drop into a state of total clinical focus that lasts 1 minute. For the duration you can't be surprised, you know the location of every unseen creature within 60 feet of you, and whenever you or a creature of your choice within 30 feet of you makes an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma saving throw, a d20 roll of 9 or lower counts as a 10. The focus ends early if you are incapacitated.
en.When you choose this domain at 1st level: When you choose this Ward at 1st level, you learn the light knack (a headlamp, penlight or chem light) if you don't already know it; it counts as a Nurse knack for you and doesn't count against your number of knacks known. Years of night shifts also give you darkvision out to 60 feet (if you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet), and within 10 feet of you, darkness created by techniques doesn't block your sight.
en.Also at 1st level, your fire and radianc: Also at 1st level, the fuel and glare you work with cling to whatever they touch. When you use a Nurse technique of 1st level or higher that deals fire or radiant damage, choose one creature that took damage from it. Until the end of your next turn, that creature smolders, shedding dim light in a 10-foot radius; it gains no benefit from being unseen, and attack rolls against it don't have disadvantage because the attacker can't see it.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one: Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one use of your Triage to light up like a sunrise. As an action, you strike a magnesium flare and thrust it high, and each hostile creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that can see you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes radiant damage equal to 2d6 + your Nurse level from the searing white glare and is blinded until the end of your next turn. On a success, it takes half as much damage and isn't blinded. The dead make this save with disadvantage. Afterward, the flare sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet for 10 minutes, and any darkness created by a technique of 3rd level or lower within that bright light is suppressed while it burns.
en.Beginning at 6th level, the same light t: Beginning at 6th level, the same heat that burns your foes keeps your friends going. You have resistance to radiant damage. In addition, when you use a Nurse technique of 1st level or higher that deals fire or radiant damage, you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you that didn't take damage from the technique. That creature gains temporary hit points equal to the technique's level + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).
en.At 8th level, sunfire follows your blows: At 8th level, heat and glare follow your blows. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or a technique attack, you can sear it for an extra 1d6 radiant damage, and it can't take the Hide action until the end of its next turn. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d6, and to 3d6 if the target is one of the dead.
en.At 17th level, your fire and radiance bu: At 17th level, your fire and glare burn at full strength. Fire and radiant damage you deal with Nurse techniques and Nurse features ignores resistance (but not immunity). In addition, when you use a Nurse technique of 1st level or higher that deals fire or radiant damage, you can use the maximum number on each damage die instead of rolling, for every target. Once you use this maximizing option, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
en.When you choose this domain at 1st level: When you choose this Ward at 1st level, you learn the druidcraft or shillelagh knack (your choice): country tricks or a good heavy stick. It counts as a Nurse knack for you and doesn't count against your knacks known. You gain proficiency in your choice of Animal Handling or Survival, and you can get simple ideas (such as danger, food, friend or follow) across to beasts through sounds and gestures; beasts understand you but can't answer in words.
en.Also at 1st level, you can call living b: Also at 1st level, you can pack a companion in a rough country poultice and wraps. As a bonus action, touch a creature (you can target yourself). It gains temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + your Nurse level, which last for 1 hour. While it has these temporary hit points, it is visibly bundled in mud-caked dressings and baling twine.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one: Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one use of your Triage to make the ground itself snare your foes. As an action, choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. You fling out coils of barbed wire and baling twine that tangle across a 15-foot-radius circle centered there for 1 minute (no concentration). Each hostile creature in the area when it appears must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your technique save DC or be restrained; a restrained creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. For the duration, the area is difficult terrain for creatures hostile to you.
en.Beginning at 6th level, the plants you s: Beginning at 6th level, your snares know friend from foe. You and creatures you choose ignore difficult terrain created by your Nurse techniques and features. In addition, as a bonus action, you can yank the wire tight around one creature within 60 feet of you that is restrained by one of your Nurse techniques or features; it takes 2d6 piercing damage. You can use this bonus action only once per turn.
en.At 8th level, your strikes carry the sti: At 8th level, your blades carry the sting of nettle and nightshade from your herb garden. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or deal damage to it with a Nurse knack, you can deal an extra 1d8 poison damage to it, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
en.At 17th level, you no longer age and can: At 17th level, tough country stock keeps you: you no longer age, and techniques can't age you. As an action, you can dig in like an old oak for 1 minute. For the duration you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage; at the start of each of your turns you regain 10 hit points if you have at least 1 hit point; and you can use Triage: Barbed Wire as a bonus action without expending a use of Triage, once during this stand. The stand ends early if you are incapacitated or you end it (no action).
en.When you choose this domain at 1st level: When you choose this Ward at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and with vehicles (water); you crewed the river rescue boat on your days off. You also have advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made to avoid being knocked prone or pushed by wind, waves or thunder (blasts and shock waves), and your cardio lets you hold your breath for twice as long as normal.
en.Also at 1st level, your storm-spells lea: Also at 1st level, your shocks leave their victims rattled. When you use a Nurse technique of 1st level or higher, each creature that takes lightning (electric) damage from it can't take reactions until the start of its next turn, and each creature that takes thunder damage from it is deafened until the end of your next turn. In addition, when you use such a technique you can move up to 10 feet immediately afterward without provoking opportunity attacks.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one: Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one use of your Triage to rig a stun pack: a car battery strapped to your back and a fistful of homemade taser darts. As an action, you power it up and immediately fire a dart at one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. On later turns, you can use a bonus action to fire another dart. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your technique save DC, taking 2d8 lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The pack holds a number of charges equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1) and dies when they are spent, after 1 minute, or if you are incapacitated. You can fire only one dart per turn.
en.Beginning at 6th level, the storm recogn: Beginning at 6th level, you know how current and shock waves travel. You have resistance to lightning and thunder damage. In addition, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you would take lightning or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to give it resistance to that damage, barking at it to let go, drop flat or cover up. Allies caught in your own shocks can be protected this way.
en.At 8th level, lightning leaps from your: At 8th level, current jumps from your strikes: a wired baton, a live blade. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or deal damage to it with a Nurse knack, the target takes an extra 1d6 lightning damage, and you can choose a second creature within 10 feet of the target that also takes 1d6 lightning damage. When you reach 14th level, both amounts increase to 2d6.
en.At 17th level, as an action you can beco: At 17th level, as an action you can go live wire for 1 minute: a frenzy of adrenaline and amperage, a live cable whipping and sparking around you. For the duration you have a speed of 60 feet for running, climbing and leaping alike, crossing walls, rooftops and gaps as if you could fly, though you must end your turn on something that holds you; and the arcing cable fills a 20-foot radius around you. A hostile creature that enters the arc for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your technique save DC or be thrown up to 15 feet away from you and knocked prone. Lightning and thunder damage you deal ignores resistance for the duration. The effect ends early if you are incapacitated.
en.When you choose this domain at 1st level: When you choose this Ward at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Deception and Sleight of Hand skills and with thieves' tools: you've talked patients down, palmed pills and picked restraint locks. You also learn the minor illusion knack (props, thrown voices and decoys); it counts as a Nurse knack for you and doesn't count against your number of knacks known.
en.Also at 1st level, you can bless a partn: Also at 1st level, you can prep a partner in mischief: a quiet word, a swipe of alcohol wipes, tape over the soles. As a bonus action, touch a creature (you can target yourself). For 10 minutes, it adds 1d4 to Dexterity (Stealth) and Charisma (Deception) checks, and it leaves no tracks or scent that can be followed by ordinary means.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one: Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one use of your Triage to swap places in the blink of an eye. As a bonus action, you and one willing creature you can see within 60 feet of you trade places in one frantic double sprint (a thrown blanket, a shout, a blur of scrubs), arriving in each other's spaces without provoking opportunity attacks. Then each hostile creature within 30 feet of either of you that saw the swap must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your technique save DC or have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn, as it loses track of which of you is which.
en.Beginning at 6th level, you are notoriou: Beginning at 6th level, you are notoriously hard to hold; you know every trick patients use to slip their restraints. You have advantage on ability checks made to escape a grapple or restraints. In addition, when you fail a saving throw against an effect that would charm (talk you into something), frighten, grapple, paralyze or restrain you, you can reroll the save and must use the new roll. Once you use this reroll, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
en.At 8th level, your god rewards a dirty t: At 8th level, you know exactly where it hurts, in body and mind. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage to it. If the target can't see you, or it is charmed or frightened, the extra damage is 2d8 instead. When you reach 14th level, these amounts increase to 2d8 and 3d8.
en.At 17th level, magic can't read your tho: At 17th level, no technique, interrogation or lie detector can read your thoughts or reveal whether you are lying unless you allow it. In addition, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can instead drop to 1 hit point, slip out of sight (you are unseen) until the start of your next turn, and scramble up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see without provoking opportunity attacks. Whatever you leave where you fell (a slumped coat, a lot of blood) passes for your body, appearing dead, for 1 minute or until a creature touches it. Once you use this escape, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
en.When you choose this domain at 1st level: When you choose this Ward at 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor. You also learn field signals: allies who can hear you can understand simple tactical commands (advance, hold, fall back, focus that target) from you even across the noise of combat and without sharing a language, thanks to whistles, hand signs and a voice that cuts through.
en.Also at 1st level, you can steady an all: Also at 1st level, you can steady an ally's aim with a barked command. When a creature other than you that you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to add 1d6 to the roll. You decide after seeing the d20 roll but before the DM says whether the attack hits. The creature must be able to hear you.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one: Starting at 2nd level, you can spend one use of your Triage to roar a battlefield order. As a bonus action, choose up to two creatures other than you within 30 feet of you that can hear you. Each of them can immediately use its reaction to make one weapon attack against a creature within its reach or range. At 10th level, each chosen creature can also move up to 10 feet before making the attack, and this movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.
en.Beginning at 6th level, you guard the li: Beginning at 6th level, you guard the line beside you. When a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage it takes from that attack by 1d10 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1), knocking the blow aside. You must be wielding a shield or a melee weapon to use this reaction, and you can't use it on yourself.
en.At 8th level, your god's verdict lands w: At 8th level, every blow you land buys someone time. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, choose one: the attack lands with bone-jarring weight for an extra 1d8 force damage, or one ally you can see within 30 feet of you gains temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier as you shout them back into the fight. When you reach 14th level, both the damage and the temporary hit point die increase to 2d8.
At 17th level, you can't be frightened. In addition, as an action you can raise your red-cross armband and rally the squad for 1 minute. For the duration, you and allies within 30 feet of you add 1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws, and once on each of your turns you can use a bonus action to let one ally within 30 feet of you who can hear you use its reaction to make one weapon attack. The rally ends early if you are incapacitated.
en.As an acolyte, you command the respect o:
You were a regular at church before the dead got up, and the faithful who are still alive remember your face. You know the prayers, the hymns and the rhythm of a service, and you can lead one when people need it. You and your companions can expect a meal, a cot and basic care wherever a congregation still holds out (a church basement, a chapel, a prayer group in someone's living room), though you must bring any supplies a treatment needs. Those who share your faith will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle.
You might also have ties to a specific church in town, and a place to sleep there. It could be the parish where you used to volunteer, if you're still on good terms with it, or one that took you in after everything fell apart. While near your church, you can ask the congregation for help, provided what you ask for isn't dangerous and you stay in their good graces.
en.You have a reliable contact who acts as: You have a reliable contact who acts as your link to what's left of the town's underworld (fences, dealers, people who move things), and you know how to get messages to and from that contact.
en.When you don't know a piece of lore, you: When you don't know something, you usually know where and from whom it can be learned: a library, an archive, a lab, the college, or someone who knows the subject.
en.Soldiers loyal to your former military o: Soldiers and veterans who served where you did still recognize your authority and influence, and you can requisition simple equipment or a vehicle for temporary use.
en.When you reach 4th level, and again at 8: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
en.Beginning at 5th level, you can attack t: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
en.You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.
en.While you are wearing armor, you gain a: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.
en.When you are wielding a melee weapon in: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
en.When a creature you can see attacks a ta: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield (a riot shield, a car door, a trash-can lid).
en.When you engage in two-weapon fighting,: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.
en.The Circle of the Land is made up of mys: Family Farm folk keep knowledge that never made it into a book: when to plant, how to read the sky, which weeds cure and which kill, passed down at kitchen tables for generations. They meet at the feed store, the church supper and the county fair, and the oldest of them are the people whole valleys go to when the well runs dry or the herd gets sick. As one of them, your know-how is shaped by the land you grew up working.
en.Druids of the Shifting Hide believe the: Vets from the Animal Clinic believe the best way to understand an animal is to work beside it, day in and day out. They spend long seasons training working dogs, sleeping in kennels and riding along on search-and-rescue calls, and they come home only when they have to. In a fight their dog is never just a pet: it is a partner that keeps going long after anyone else would have quit.
en.Drawing on the divine essence of nature: Drawing on a lifetime of farm and animal know-how, you can use techniques that bend the land, the weather and the animals around you to your purpose.
en.You know Druidic, the secret language of: You know the old country signs: knots in fence wire, stacked stones, a notch cut in a post, a rag tied a certain way. You can read them and use them to leave hidden messages. You and others who grew up on the land automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can't decipher it unless someone teaches them the signs.
en.Wild Shape (CR 1/4 or below, no flying o: Loyal Dog (young dog, CR 1/4 or below)
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can use your:
Starting at 2nd level, a dog has thrown in its lot with you: a farm dog, a stray you fed, an old patient from the clinic. It follows you everywhere, but it only throws itself into danger when you call it in. You can use your action to rally your dog. You can use this feature twice. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
Your Farmer level determines how capable your dog is, as shown in the Loyal Dog table. At 2nd level, for example, it is a young dog roughly equal to a creature with a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower. The DM sets its exact statistics and decides what it can and can't do.
A rally lasts for a number of hours equal to half your Farmer level (rounded down). The dog then settles back at heel unless you expend another use of this feature. You can call it off earlier by using a bonus action on your turn. The rally ends automatically if you fall unconscious, drop to 0 hit points, or die.
While your dog is rallied, the following rules apply:
- The dog acts on your turn and follows your spoken commands and whistles. It uses its own statistics, set by the DM, and it is still a dog: it can't do anything a real dog couldn't. It adds your proficiency bonus to any skill or saving throw you are proficient in if its own bonus for that roll is lower.
- The dog has its own hit points and Hit Dice. While it is right beside you, it can throw itself in the way of a hit meant for you: the dog takes the damage instead of you. If that drops it to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to you. For example, if the dog has only 1 hit point left and takes 10 damage for you, it goes down and you take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce you to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious. A downed dog is out of the fight until you finish a long rest; it dies only if the DM rules the blow was clearly lethal.
- Handling the dog doesn't stop you from talking or using your hands, and it doesn't break your concentration on a technique you've already started or stop you from continuing a technique that is already under way.
- You keep the benefit of all your features from your profession, origin, or any other source. The dog has its own senses: it can smell the dead long before you see them, and the DM tells you when it growls.
- You choose what gear the dog wears: a harness, saddlebags, a padded vest. Worn gear works as normal, but the DM decides whether a piece of equipment is practical for the dog, based on its size and build. Equipment doesn't change size or shape to fit it, and anything the dog can't wear stays with you.
en.At 2nd level, you choose to identify wit: At 2nd level, you choose the kind of homestead you come from, such as the Family Farm. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.
en.When you choose this circle at 2nd level: When you choose this homestead at 2nd level, you learn one additional Farmer knack of your choice.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can regain so:
Starting at 2nd level, you can get some of your edge back by sitting quietly outside for a while, listening to the wind and the fields until your head clears. During a short rest, you choose expended technique slots to recover. The technique slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your Farmer level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level Farmer, you can recover up to two levels worth of technique slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level slot or two 1st-level slots.
en.Your mystical connection to the land inf:
Years of working your land taught you tricks no one else around here knows. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to farm techniques tied to the land where you grew up.
Choose that land--cold country, coast, desert, forest, prairie, mountain, or swamp--and consult the associated list of techniques.
Once you gain access to a farm technique, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of techniques you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a technique that doesn't appear on the Farmer technique list, the technique is nonetheless a Farmer technique for you.
en.Wild Shape (CR 1/2 or below, no flying s: Loyal Dog (grown dog, CR 1/2 or below)
en.Starting at 6th level, moving through no:
Starting at 6th level, moving through ordinary difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through brush, crops and undergrowth without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, barbed wire, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against vines, nets and snares that someone has rigged to impede movement, such as those created by the tangle-line technique.
en.Wild Shape (CR 1 or below): Loyal Dog (seasoned dog, CR 1 or below)
en.When you reach 10th level, you can't be: When you reach 10th level, you can't be talked into things or frightened by wild animals or the dead, and you are immune to poison and disease.
en.When you reach 14th level, creatures of: When you reach 14th level, animals sense that you are one of the good ones and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Farmer technique save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours. The creature is aware of this effect before it makes its attack against you.
en.Starting at 18th level, the primal magic: Starting at 18th level, a hard life of clean air, heavy work and plain food has made you age more slowly. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.
en.Beginning at 18th level, you can cast ma: Beginning at 18th level, you and your dog work as one. While your dog is rallied with Loyal Dog, it can deliver any of your Farmer techniques that have a range of touch, carrying a snare, a dressing or a dose to its target in its jaws. You still say the words and make the gestures, but the dog can't supply anything for you: you must have any supplies the technique needs.
en.At 20th level, you can use your Wild Sha:
At 20th level, you can use your Loyal Dog an unlimited number of times.
Additionally, you can use your Farmer techniques without speaking or gesturing, and without any supplies that have no cost and aren't used up by the technique. You gain this benefit whether or not your dog is rallied with Loyal Dog.
en.When you join this circle at 2nd level,:
When you join this clinic at 2nd level, rallying your dog comes as easily as breathing. You can use Loyal Dog as a bonus action on your turn instead of an action.
Your dog is also a bigger, better-trained working breed than most. Use the following table in place of the Loyal Dog table's challenge rating limit (the DM still decides what a real dog of that kind can do):
Farmer level 2nd–3rd: max CR 1/2
Farmer level 4th–5th: max CR 1
Farmer level 6th–7th: max CR 2
Farmer level 8th–11th: max CR 3
Farmer level 12th–15th: max CR 4
Farmer level 16th–19th: max CR 5
Farmer level 20th: max CR 6
en.Also at 2nd level, you can draw on your: Also at 2nd level, you can treat your dog in the middle of a fight. While your dog is rallied with Loyal Dog, you can use a bonus action to expend one Farmer technique slot and restore hit points to your dog equal to 1d6 per level of the expended slot + your Farmer level. In addition, when you rally your dog with Loyal Dog, it gains temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1); they vanish when the rally ends.
en.Starting at 6th level, your attacks in b: Starting at 6th level, your dog's bites and charges punch through resistance and immunity that stop ordinary attacks. In addition, your training guides each strike: when your dog makes an attack roll with its bite or claws, you can use your Wisdom modifier in place of the dog's Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack roll (not the damage roll), and it adds your proficiency bonus if yours is higher than its own.
en.At 10th level, you can wear the shape of: At 10th level, you can turn the animals of a whole farm loose on your enemies. As an action, you can expend one use of Loyal Dog together with a Farmer technique slot of 4th level or higher to drive a stampede into the fight: a panicked herd of cattle, a bull, a pack of half-wild farm dogs, or whatever animals the place has. The DM picks a fitting stat block of about challenge rating five, and you direct it as you would your dog. The stampede follows the normal Loyal Dog rules, except that it lasts for at most 10 minutes and you can't use Working Dog to start it as a bonus action. Once per long rest you can start a stampede by expending only the Loyal Dog use, with no technique slot.
en.At 14th level, there is always another s: At 14th level, your dog always has a little more in it. When your dog is reduced to 0 hit points while rallied with Loyal Dog, you can use your reaction to bark one sharp command: it staggers back to its feet with the hit points of a fresh rally instead of going down. This doesn't expend a use of Loyal Dog; any excess damage is lost rather than carrying over to you. Once you use this reaction, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest. In addition, while your dog is rallied, it can deliver Farmer techniques of 3rd level or lower that need no supplies, as if you had reached the Working Together feature early.
en.The archetypal Champion focuses on the d: Infantry soldiers are built on one idea: raw physical toughness, drilled until it becomes second nature. Years of ruck marches, live-fire ranges and close-quarters drills turned an ordinary body into a weapon that hits hard and keeps going when everyone else is spent.
en.Warlords treat every skirmish as a puzzl: Sergeants treat every skirmish as a puzzle of angles, timing, and nerve. They fight at the front of the line, reading the street and calling the moves that turn a brawl into a rout, and the people around them learn to listen when the Sergeant barks an order.
en.Spellblades never sat through a wizard's: Combat Engineers never sat through a chemistry degree; they learned a handful of field-proven builds by heart and taped, wired and bolted them onto the gear they carry. Their bag of tricks is small and specialised but always ready, worked in between swings of a weapon rather than read from a manual.
en.You adopt a particular style of fighting: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your trademark. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
en.When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die f: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.
en.You have a limited well of stamina that: You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to keep yourself in the fight. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your Soldier level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
en.Starting at 2nd level, you can push your:
Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action and a possible bonus action.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.
en.At 3rd level, you choose an archetype th: At 3rd level, you choose a specialty from your time in uniform that shapes how you fight, such as Infantry. The specialty you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.
en.Beginning when you choose this archetype: Beginning when you choose this specialty at 3rd level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
en.When you reach 4th level, and again at 6: When you reach 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
en.Beginning at 5th level, you can attack t: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level as a Soldier and to four when you reach 20th level as a Soldier.
en.Starting at 7th level, you can add half: Starting at 7th level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus. In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier.
en.Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a: Beginning at 9th level, you can grit your teeth and reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest. You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level and three times between long rests starting at 17th level.
en.At 10th level, you can choose a second o: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style feature.
en.Starting at 15th level, your weapon atta: Starting at 15th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.
en.At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle o: At 18th level, you reach the peak of combat endurance: you have been hurt so many times that your body simply refuses to quit. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.
en.You carry a reserve of battlefield insti: You carry a reserve of hard-won battlefield instinct represented by tactics dice, which are d8s. Your number of tactics dice equals 1 + your proficiency bonus (tracked on your sheet). A tactics die is expended when you use it to fuel a Sergeant maneuver, and you regain all expended tactics dice when you finish a short or long rest. The die becomes a d10 at 10th level and a d12 at 18th level.
en.You learn three maneuvers of your choice: You learn three maneuvers of your choice from the list below; you learn one more at 7th, 10th, and 15th level. Whenever you gain a Soldier level you can replace one maneuver you know with another. Using a maneuver expends one tactics die, and you can apply only one maneuver to a single attack or trigger. If a maneuver calls for a saving throw, the DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). Maneuvers: • Crack the Guard (on a hit): add the tactics die to the damage roll, and the target takes a -1 penalty to AC until the start of your next turn (this penalty doesn't stack with itself). • Hamstring (on a hit): add the tactics die to the damage roll; the target's speed is reduced by 15 feet and it can't take reactions until the start of your next turn. • Overrun (on a hit with a melee attack): add the tactics die to the damage roll. A target that is no more than one size larger than you must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet straight away from you; you can then move up to 10 feet after it without provoking opportunity attacks. • Steady Hand (before you make an attack roll): add the tactics die to the attack roll. If the attack still misses, the die is not expended. • Body Block (reaction, when a creature you can see hits you or an ally within 5 feet of you): roll the tactics die and reduce the damage of that hit by the number rolled + your Constitution modifier (minimum reduction 1). • Exploit Opening (on a hit): mark the target until the start of your next turn. The next attack roll an ally makes against it during that time adds your tactics die to its damage roll and ignores half cover. • On Me! (bonus action): choose one ally within 30 feet who can see or hear you. It gains temporary hit points equal to your tactics die roll + your proficiency bonus, and it can immediately use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. • Iron Resolve (when you fail a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw): roll the tactics die and add it to the saving throw, possibly turning the failure into a success.
en.Your study of warfare pays off off the b: Your years in the service pay off away from the fight too. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: History, Insight, Intimidation, or Persuasion. In addition, you can't be surprised while you are conscious and at least one ally you can see is not surprised, as you instinctively shout a warning to each other.
en.As a bonus action, you size up one creat: As a bonus action, you size up one creature you can see within 60 feet. The DM tells you its Armor Class, roughly how wounded it is (unhurt, bloodied, or near death), and either its highest saving throw or one damage resistance or immunity it has (your choice). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest. You also learn a fourth Sergeant maneuver.
en.Your tactics dice become d10s. You also: Your tactics dice become d10s. You also learn one additional Sergeant maneuver. In addition, when you roll initiative, you can choose one ally within 30 feet who can see or hear you: that ally adds your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) to its initiative roll as you call out the opening move.
en.Once per turn, when you score a critical: Once per turn, when you score a critical hit or reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points with a weapon attack, you regain one expended tactics die. You also learn one additional Sergeant maneuver, bringing the total you know to six (3 + one each at 7th, 10th, and 15th level).
en.Your tactics dice become d12s. In additi: Your tactics dice become d12s. In addition, once on each of your turns you can apply two different maneuvers to the same attack or trigger, expending one tactics die for each. Finally, if you roll initiative and have no tactics dice remaining, you regain two of them.
en.You gain innate arcane magic. Intelligen: You carry a kit of small, field-built devices and know them by heart. Intelligence is your technique ability for every technique you use with Combat Engineer features: your technique save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier, and your technique attack modifier is your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. You don't use technique slots; techniques used through these features are used at their lowest level, need no supplies unless the technique lists an item with a cost that it uses up, and can't be boosted to a higher level. You know two knacks of your choice from this list and can use them at will: Bleeder, Flare Shot, Work Light, Grabber Pole, Multitool, Freeze Spray, Live Wire, Range Finder.
en.You hold a small reservoir of stored pow: You keep a few devices pre-built and ready to go. Choose two of the following 1st-level techniques: Torch Burst, Sweep, Hustle, Stim Shot, Vault, Nail Gun, Concussion Charge. You always know Brace as well. You can expend one charge to use Brace or one of your chosen techniques at 1st level without a technique slot. You have a number of charges equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) and regain them all on a long rest, rebuilding them from scrap. When you gain a Soldier level you can swap one chosen technique for another on the list.
en.During a short or long rest, you can etc: During a short or long rest, you can rig one weapon you are proficient with: a wrist lanyard, a locking grip and a retractable steel cable spooled to your belt. Any check or effect that would make you drop it or take it from your grip automatically fails while you are conscious. You can use it as your tools for techniques and keep working with your hands while holding it. As a bonus action, you can reel the weapon back to your hand if it is within 30 feet of you and not held or carried by another creature. You can have only one rigged weapon; rigging a new one ends the old rig.
en.Once per turn, when you hit a creature w: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with your rigged weapon as part of the Attack action, the small charge built into it goes off and the strike deals extra force damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1), and you can then use one knack you know from Field Kit as a bonus action that turn (the knack must normally take 1 action to use). If the knack requires an attack roll or saving throw, it must target the creature you hit or a creature within 10 feet of it.
en.You learn two 2nd-level spells of your c: You learn two 2nd-level techniques of your choice from this list: Smoke Cloak, Weapon Mod, Decoys, Smoke and Dash, Thermal Scope, Shaped Charge. You can use either of them at 2nd level without a technique slot, using Intelligence as your technique ability. You can do so twice in total, regaining both uses when you finish a long rest. Alternatively, you can expend two charges from Ready Charges to use one of these techniques.
en.Your bonded weapon cuts at the threads o: Every hit from your rigged weapon rattles teeth and scrambles plans. When you hit a creature that is concentrating on a technique with your rigged weapon, it makes its concentration saving throw with disadvantage. In addition, after you hit a creature with your rigged weapon, you have advantage on saving throws against techniques and other effects that creature creates until the start of your next turn.
en.You learn two 3rd-level spells of your c: You learn two 3rd-level techniques of your choice from this list: Ghosting, Disrupt, Grapple Rig, Combat Stims, Live Line, Hazmat Gear. You can use one of them at 3rd level without a technique slot, using Intelligence as your technique ability; you can do so twice, regaining both uses when you finish a long rest. Each time you gain a Soldier level you can swap one of these techniques for another from the list.
Tools and weapons are one motion for you. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with a knack you know from Field Kit that takes 1 action to use. In addition, whenever you use Action Surge, you regain one expended charge from Ready Charges, and your next rigged-weapon hit that turn deals an extra 2d8 force damage.
en.Monks of the Way of the Open Hand are th: Coaches of the Dojo discipline are the purest students of hand-to-hand combat, armed or unarmed. They learn throws and sweeps to push and trip their opponents, the breathing and focus to work through their own injuries, and a calm under pressure that keeps them out of harm's way.
en.Monks of the Dusk keep their vigils in t: Street Style fighters learned in parking garages, alleys and night shifts, in the hour when the streetlights fail. They teach that the dark is not an absence but a place you can stand in, hide in and strike from. Their students are watchers, bouncers, night guards, and occasionally the quiet end of someone who had it coming.
en.Practitioners of the Tempered Elements f: Muay Thai fighters forge their bodies the way a smith works metal: shins hardened on heavy bags, lungs burned on hill sprints, nerves numbed by a thousand clinches. Each move is a strict discipline drilled until it's reflex, and in the dead town they've added whatever the fight needs: a lit flare in a wrapped fist, a stun knuckle, a kick that kills a leg. Masters chain several into a single flowing combination.
en.Beginning at 1st level, while you are we: Beginning at 1st level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier. Years of sparring taught you to slip, read and roll with every blow.
en.At 1st level, your practice of martial a:
At 1st level, your years on the mat give you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and training weapons, which are shortswords (machetes, big knives) and any simple melee weapons that don't have the two- handed or heavy property.
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only training weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield:
- You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and training weapons.
- You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or training weapon. This die changes as you gain Martial-Arts Coach levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of Table: The Martial-Arts Coach.
- When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a training weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn.
Every gym has its own version of the training weapons. For example, you might use a club that is two lengths of wood connected by a short chain (a nunchaku), an escrima stick, a tonfa, or a sharpened garden sickle (a kama). Whatever you call your training weapon, you can use the game statistics provided for the weapon.
en.Starting at 2nd level, your training all:
Starting at 2nd level, your training lets you dig into reserves most people never reach: breath control, pain tolerance, perfect timing. Your access to these reserves is represented by a number of focus points. Your Martial-Arts Coach level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Focus Points column of Table: The Martial-Arts Coach.
You can spend these points to fuel various focus features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more focus features as you gain levels in this class.
When you spend a focus point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you have pulled yourself back together. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest breathing, stretching or meditating to regain your focus points.
Some of your focus features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Focus save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
en.Immediately after you take the Attack ac: Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 focus point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.
en.You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dod: You can spend 1 focus point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action on your turn.
en.You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dis: You can spend 1 focus point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.
en.Starting at 2nd level, your speed increa:
Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain Martial-Arts Coach levels, as shown in Table: The Martial-Arts Coach.
