At 9th level, your parkour is good enough to move along vertical surfaces (wall runs, fences, the sides of trucks) and across liquids and footing that shouldn't hold you (flood water, mud, thin ice, sagging roofs) on your turn without falling during the move.
en.When you reach 3rd level, you commit you: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a discipline, such as Dojo. Your discipline grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.
en.Starting at 3rd level, you can use your:
Starting at 3rd level, you can use your reaction to slap aside, dodge or blunt the hit when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Martial-Arts Coach level.
If you reduce the damage to 0, you can catch the missile if it is small enough for you to hold in one hand, you have at least one hand free, and it isn't a bullet (thrown knives, bricks, arrows and bolts, yes; gunfire, never). If you catch a missile in this way, you can spend 1 focus point to make a ranged attack with the weapon or piece of ammunition you just caught, as part of the same reaction. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and the missile counts as a training weapon for the attack, which has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.
en.Starting when you choose this tradition:
Starting when you choose this discipline at 3rd level, you can use your opponent's balance and momentum against them. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target:
- It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
- It must make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, you can push it up to 15 feet away from you.
- It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.
en.Beginning at 4th level, you can use your: Beginning at 4th level, you can use your reaction when you fall to tuck, roll and spread the impact, reducing any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your Martial-Arts Coach level.
en.Starting at 5th level, you can interfere: Starting at 5th level, you know exactly where to hit: the jaw hinge, the temple, the solar plexus. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 focus point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.
en.Starting at 6th level, your unarmed stri: Starting at 6th level, your conditioned hands, elbows and shins hit like weapons: your unarmed strikes punch through resistance and immunity that stop ordinary attacks.
en.At 6th level, you gain the ability to he: At 6th level, you learn to work through your own injuries: you breathe, reset a joint, tape what needs taping and keep going. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your Martial-Arts Coach level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.
en.At 7th level, your instinctive agility l: At 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a grenade blast or a car going up in flames. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
en.Starting at 7th level, you can use your: Starting at 7th level, you can use your action to breathe, reset and shake off one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed (talked into something) or frightened.
en.At 10th level, your mastery of the ki fl: At 10th level, your conditioning and discipline make you immune to disease and poison. (Whether that covers the bite of the dead is the DM's call.)
en.Beginning at 11th level, you can enter a: Beginning at 11th level, you can settle into a deep calm that makes others hesitate to lay a hand on you. At the end of a long rest, you gain the following effect, which lasts until the start of your next long rest: any creature that targets you with an attack or a harmful technique must first make a Wisdom saving throw; on a failure, it must choose a new target or lose the attack or technique. The effect ends early if you make an attack or use a technique that affects an enemy. The saving throw DC equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus.
en.Starting at 13th level, you learn to tou: Starting at 13th level, you have coached people from everywhere, and you read tone, gesture and intent so well that you understand the meaning of any spoken language. Moreover, any creature that can understand a language can understand what you mean, through words, mime and sheer clarity.
en.Beginning at 14th level, your mastery of:
Beginning at 14th level, your discipline grants you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 focus point to reroll it and take the second result.
en.At 15th level, your ki sustains you so t: At 15th level, your training keeps you in fighting shape, so you suffer none of the frailty of old age. You can still die of old age, however. In addition, your body runs on almost nothing: you no longer need food or water.
en.At 17th level, you gain the ability to s:
At 17th level, you learn the forbidden strike: a precise blow that leaves a hidden internal injury in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 focus points to set up this imperceptible injury, which lasts for a number of days equal to your Martial-Arts Coach level. The injury is harmless unless you use your action to set it off, wherever the target is. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it is reduced to 0 hit points. If it succeeds, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage as something inside it gives way.
You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can choose to let the injury heal harmlessly without using an action.
en.Beginning at 18th level, you can use you:
Beginning at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 4 focus points to move so cleanly and quietly that eyes slide right off you: you are invisible for 1 minute. During that time, you also roll with every blow, giving you resistance to all damage but force damage.
Additionally, you can spend 8 focus points to vanish from a scene entirely, alone: you slip away unseen and untracked, and the DM lets you turn up later anywhere you could plausibly have reached on foot. You can't take any other creatures with you.
en.At 20th level, when you roll for initiat: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have no focus points remaining, you regain 4 focus points.
en.As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki po: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 focus point to melt into the gloom for 1 minute: hood up, dark clothes, staying low and out of the light. While you keep this low profile, you are lightly obscured to other creatures, you can take the Hide action even while only lightly obscured, and opportunity attacks made against you while you are in dim light or darkness have disadvantage. The effect ends early if you are in bright light at the end of your turn.
en.You gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or i: Years of night shifts have trained your eyes: you gain darkvision out to 60 feet, or increase the range of your existing darkvision by 30 feet. In addition, as an action you can spend 3 focus points to kill the lights around a point within 60 feet (smash a bulb, pull a breaker, pop a black-smoke canister), creating darkness there as the darkness technique does, without spending a technique slot. You fight normally inside darkness you create this way, and while you remain inside its area it doesn't require your concentration (it ends early if you leave the area).
en.When you use Step of the Wind, you can s: When you use Step of the Wind, you can spend 1 additional focus point to make a sudden dash or vault instead of moving normally: you drop out of sight and reappear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet that is in dim light or darkness. Until the end of that turn, the first melee attack you make against a creature that was not within 5 feet of you before the dash has advantage.
en.As a bonus action, you can spend 3 ki po: As a bonus action, you can spend 3 focus points to vanish into the dark for 1 minute: you become invisible. This only works while you are in dim light or darkness; whenever you are in bright light you are visible, but the effect doesn't end. The effect ends early if you hit a creature with an attack, after the attack is resolved, or if you are incapacitated.
en.As an action, you can spend 5 ki points: As an action, you can spend 5 focus points to plunge everything within 20 feet of you into total darkness for 1 minute, a pall of smoke, soot and smashed lights that moves with you and that not even darkvision can see through; you can see through it. While it lasts, whenever a creature inside the sphere makes an attack roll against a target other than you, you can use your reaction to make one unarmed strike against that creature if it is within your reach, and that strike deals an extra 2d6 necrotic damage on a hit as you crush a throat or a spine.
en.You learn two elemental techniques of yo: You learn two Muay Thai moves of your choice from the list below, and one more at 6th, 11th, and 17th level. Whenever you gain a Martial-Arts Coach level, you can swap one move you know for another. Each move costs the listed focus points. Saving throws use your focus save DC (8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier). You can apply only one on-hit move to a single strike. In this style, fire damage comes from a lit flare or lighter in your wrapped fist, cold damage is a numbing strike that kills a nerve, lightning damage is a stun knuckle wired into your wraps, and thunder damage is pure concussive force. Moves: • Burning Elbow (1 focus, when you hit with an unarmed strike, once per turn): the strike deals an extra 1d10 fire damage, and the target's clothes smolder: it sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius and can't benefit from being invisible until the start of your next turn. • Dead Leg (1 focus, when you hit with an unarmed strike, once per turn): the strike deals an extra 1d8 cold damage and the target's speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. • Clinch Throw (1 focus, when you hit with an unarmed strike, once per turn): the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 15 feet toward you or pushed up to 15 feet away from you (your choice); a Large or smaller creature that fails by 5 or more is also knocked prone. • Iron Guard (1 focus, bonus action): until the start of your next turn you gain +2 AC and can't be pushed, pulled, or knocked prone against your will. • Flying Knee (1 focus, bonus action): you launch yourself off walls, cars and railings, gaining a flying speed equal to your walking speed until the end of your turn; if you are still off the ground then, you drop and land safely. • Crowd Breaker (2 focus, action): you stomp, shove and elbow out in every direction; you use the thunderwave technique without spending a technique slot, using your focus save DC. • Live Wire (1 focus, when you use Step of the Wind): the first creature you move within 5 feet of during that movement must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d8 lightning damage.
en.You learn one additional elemental techn: You learn one additional Muay Thai move. When you finish a long rest, choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder: you've hardened yourself against that kind of punishment (chemical burns, numbing cold, burns, electric shocks or blasts) and have resistance to that damage type until your next long rest. In addition, when you hit with an unarmed strike, you can have it deal cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage instead of bludgeoning.
en.You learn one additional technique, whic: You learn one additional move, which can be chosen from the basic list or from the advanced moves below (advanced moves can be learned from now on whenever you gain a move). Advanced moves: • Surge Line (4 focus, action, 11th level): you jam a stripped cable from the battery pack in your kit into anything that conducts (a wet gutter, a chain-link fence, a downed line) and send current along a 100-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line. Each creature in the line makes a Dexterity save, taking 6d8 lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. • Leg-Kick Circle (4 focus, action, 11th level): you spin through a circuit of brutal low kicks; each creature of your choice within 15 feet of you makes a Constitution save, taking 5d8 cold damage and having its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn on a failure, or half damage and no speed loss on a success. • Cover Up (3 focus, reaction, 11th level): when you or a creature within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack, you step in to block or smother the blow, reducing the damage by 2d10 + your Wisdom modifier.
en.You learn one additional technique. As a: You learn one additional move. As a bonus action, you can spend 5 focus points to enter the zone for 1 minute, every strike in your arsenal live. Choose cold, fire, lightning, or thunder: you have resistance to that type and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from ordinary attacks, your unarmed strikes deal an extra 1d6 damage of the chosen type, and every Muay Thai move costs 1 fewer focus point (minimum 1).
en.The Oath of Devotion binds a paladin to: The Protect & Serve badge binds an officer to the oldest ideals of the job: justice, decency and order. Some call them boy scouts or straight arrows; they are the cop from the recruiting poster, acting with honor in pursuit of justice and the greater good. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some, for better or worse, hold the rest of the world to the same standards. Many who wear this badge measure themselves against the code they swore at the academy, a parent who wore the uniform before them, or a faith they keep quietly. Now that the dispatcher has gone silent, they still answer every call.
en.Paladins of the Evergreen swear to shelt: Park Rangers swear to shelter what grows: the woods along the river, the fields, the kids, the small bright joys that make a life worth living. Their code is to tend before they take, to keep hope alive where it gutters, and to stand against rot in every form, whether disease, the dead or plain cruelty. They still wear the flat hat and the green uniform, patched now, with a radio nobody answers clipped to the shoulder.
en.An Oath of Retribution is sworn over the: Homicide detectives work over the ashes of something terrible. The ones still on the job now hunt killers, raiders and the people who feed others to the dead, holding that a wrong left unanswered will be repeated. Their code is to name the guilty, to never close a case unsolved, and to make the punishment fit the crime, though some lose themselves in the chase and stop telling the difference between justice and revenge.
en.The presence of strong evil registers on:
Something wrong registers on your senses like a bad smell, and years on patrol taught you to trust it. As an action, you can stop, listen and read the scene. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any of the dead within 60 feet of you that is not behind total cover, and of anyone lying in wait for you in that area. You know whether each presence you sense is living or dead, but not its identity. Within the same radius, you also notice any place or object that bears the marks of violence or has been deliberately marked (a kill site, a hidden stash, a gang tag).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.
en.Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You:
Your first-aid training can patch up wounds. You have a pool of first-aid capacity that replenishes when you take a long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your Police Officer level x 5.
As an action, you can treat a creature you touch, drawing on the pool to restore a number of hit points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool.
Alternatively, you can expend 5 hit points from your pool to treat the target for one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it (antibiotics, activated charcoal, an epinephrine shot). You can treat multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of First Responder, expending hit points separately for each one.
This feature has no effect on the dead or on machines.
en.At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fight: At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
en.When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die f: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.
en.By 2nd level, you have learned to draw o: By 2nd level, academy drills, field training and long nights on patrol let you use techniques, preparing them the way a Nurse does.
en.Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a cr: Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one technique slot to turn the hit into a brutal, textbook takedown and deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level technique slot, plus 1d8 for each technique level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is one of the dead.
en.By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing t: By 3rd level, your fitness tests, vaccinations and sheer stubbornness make you immune to disease. (Whether that covers the bite of the dead is the DM's call.)
en.When you reach 3rd level, you swear the:
When you reach 3rd level, you pin on the badge that defines you as an officer for good. Up to this time you have been a rookie, committed to the job but not yet sure what kind of cop you are. Now you choose a badge, such as Protect & Serve.
Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. Those features include badge techniques and the Triage feature.
en.Each oath has a list of associated spell:
Each badge has a list of associated techniques. You gain access to these techniques at the levels specified in the badge description. Once you gain access to a badge technique, you always have it prepared. Badge techniques don't count against the number of techniques you can prepare each day.
If you gain a badge technique that doesn't appear on the Police Officer technique list, the technique is nonetheless a Police Officer technique for you.
en.Your oath allows you to channel divine e:
Your badge gives you ways to take control of a scene when everything goes wrong. Each Triage option provided by your badge explains how to use it.
When you use your Triage, you choose which option to use. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Triage again.
Some Triage effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your Police Officer technique save DC.
en.As an action, you can imbue one weapon t:
As an action, you can square up with one weapon that you are holding, using your Triage. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). A mounted tactical light on the weapon also emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that. For the duration, attacks with the weapon punch through resistance and immunity that stop ordinary attacks.
You can end this effect on your turn as part of any other action. If you are no longer holding or carrying this weapon, or if you fall unconscious, this effect ends.
en.As an action, you present your holy symb:
As an action, you hit the strobes and the siren, or bark through a bullhorn, using your Triage. Each of the dead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.
A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.
en.Starting at 6th level, whenever you or a:
Starting at 6th level, your voice cuts through panic: whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you must make a saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
en.Starting at 7th level, you and friendly:
Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed (talked into things) while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
en.Starting at 10th level, you and friendly:
Starting at 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
en.By 11th level, you are so suffused with: By 11th level, every swing you take is trained, practiced and meant to end the fight. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d8 radiant damage. If you also use your Takedown with an attack, you add this damage to the extra damage of your Takedown.
en.Beginning at 14th level, you can use you:
Beginning at 14th level, you can use your action to end one technique affecting yourself or one willing creature that you touch: cut the zip ties, flush the pepper spray, snap them out of it.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.
en.Beginning at 15th level, you are always: Beginning at 15th level, you are permanently on guard against the dead: they have disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and you can't be charmed, frightened, or possessed by them.
en.At 18th level, the range of your auras i: At 18th level, the range of your auras increase to 30 feet.
en.At 20th level, as an action, you can ema:
At 20th level, as an action, you can light up the scene and bring everything you have to bear: floodlights, flashbangs, the cruiser's spotlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against techniques used by hostile creatures, living or dead.
en.You can spend one use of your Channel Di: You can spend one use of your Triage to break out the trail kit: water, electrolytes, antivenom, a few words that get people back on their feet. As an action, choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1); you can include yourself. Each chosen creature gains temporary hit points equal to your Police Officer level + your Charisma modifier, and you can end either the poisoned condition or one disease on each of them.

You can spend one use of your Triage to turn the drip torch you carry for controlled burns on the things that rot the world. As an action, each of the dead of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against your technique save DC. On a failure, it takes radiant damage equal to 2d8 + your Police Officer level and its speed is halved for 1 minute; it can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the slowing on a success. On a success, it takes half the damage and isn't slowed.
en.Starting at 7th level, you and friendly: Starting at 7th level, you know which water is safe, which plants will make you sick and how to set up a clean camp: you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned. In addition, whenever a creature in the aura regains hit points from a technique or other special effect, it regains extra hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). You must be conscious to grant these benefits. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
en.Beginning at 15th level, you endure like: Beginning at 15th level, you endure like an old oak. At the start of each of your turns, if you have at least 1 hit point but no more than half your hit point maximum, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Charisma modifier. In addition, you suffer none of the drawbacks of old age, and you need only half as much food and water as normal.
en.At 18th level, your shelter spreads like: At 18th level, your shelter spreads like the crown of a great tree. The range of your Safe Camp and your Command Presence increases from 10 feet to 30 feet. The aura's benefits still apply only to friendly creatures and only while you are conscious.
en.At 20th level, as an action you can beco: At 20th level, as an action you can become the woods themselves for 1 minute. Brush, bark and a ghillie wrap cover your body, granting a +2 bonus to AC. At the start of each of your turns, you pass out water and gauze and keep everyone moving: you and each friendly creature in your aura regain 10 hit points (a creature at 0 hit points isn't affected). Any hostile creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your technique save DC or be restrained by snares and tangled roots until the start of its next turn. Ground within 30 feet of you is difficult terrain for hostile creatures. The effect ends early if you are incapacitated.
en.You can spend one use of your Channel Di: You can spend one use of your Triage to make a suspect your case. As a bonus action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. For 1 hour, or until it drops to 0 hit points, the creature is marked: you've profiled it so well that it gains no benefit from being invisible against you, you know its direction and distance while it is within 1 mile of you, and once on each of your turns when you hit it with a weapon attack, you deal extra radiant damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

You can spend one use of your Triage to answer violence immediately. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you deals damage to you or to a friendly creature, you can use your reaction to come down on it hard, forcing it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your technique save DC. On a failure, it takes radiant damage equal to 2d8 + your Police Officer level and is frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On a success, it takes half as much damage and isn't frightened.
en.Starting at 7th level, you project an au: Starting at 7th level, you carry yourself with an unforgiving edge that your partners pick up on. While you are conscious, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have advantage on opportunity attacks, and hostile creatures within the aura regain only half the normal number of hit points from any healing. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
en.Beginning at 15th level, nothing turns y: Beginning at 15th level, nothing turns you from the hunt. You are immune to the frightened condition. In addition, when you use Takedown against a creature marked by your Triage: Person of Interest, the Takedown's damage dice are d10s instead of d8s, and the marked creature has disadvantage on saving throws against your Police Officer techniques.
en.At 18th level, your judgment reaches far: At 18th level, your reach extends farther. The range of your No Mercy and your Command Presence increases from 10 feet to 30 feet. In addition, your Triage: Use of Force can target a creature up to 60 feet away instead of 30 feet.
en.At 20th level, as an action you can beco: At 20th level, as an action you can go all-in on the hunt for 1 minute. Your radio crackles, your flashlight sweeps, and you do not stop. For the duration, you can use a bonus action on each of your turns to apply Person of Interest to a creature without expending Triage (up to three creatures marked at once), your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 against marked creatures, and a marked creature that ends its turn within 30 feet of you takes 2d10 radiant damage. The effect ends early if you are incapacitated.
en.Emulating the Hunter archetype means acc: Big Game hunters accept their place as the line between what is left of town and whatever comes out of the trees. As you follow this style, you learn specialized ways of bringing down the threats you face, from lone bruisers twice your size and swarms of the dead to raider gangs that move like a pack.
en.A Packbond Warden never walks the wild a: A Pack Hunter never works the woods alone. Through months of shared hunts, scraps from the same plate and nights by the same fire, the hunter bonds with a single animal that becomes partner, scout, and shield. The pair hunts as one creature with two bodies, each covering the other's blind side.
en.Beginning at 1st level, you have signifi:
Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.
Choose a type of prey: mutants, animals, zealots, machines, apex predators, firebugs, drifters, cultists, brutes, freaks, crawlers, mold, or the dead. Alternatively, you can select two groups of people (such as raiders and bikers) as your prey.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your chosen prey, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.
When you gain this feature, you also learn one language or dialect of your choice that is spoken by your chosen prey, if they speak one at all.
You choose one additional prey, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the kinds of threats you have run into out there.
en.You are particularly familiar with one t:
You are particularly familiar with one type of outdoor country and are adept at traveling and surviving in it. Choose one type of favored terrain: snow country, lakeshore, badlands, woods, open fields, high country, or bottomlands. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.
While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:
- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
- Your group can't become lost unless someone deliberately misleads you.
- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.
You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.
en.At 2nd level, you adopt a particular sty: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
en.By the time you reach 2nd level, you hav: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have picked up the old field craft of the woods (snares, scent, sign, and patience) and can put it to use as techniques, much as a farmer or vet does.
en.At 3rd level, you choose an archetype th: At 3rd level, you choose a Hunting Style that you strive to master, such as Big Game. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.
en.At 3rd level, you gain one of the follow:
At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Wear Them Down
Bring Down the Big Ones
Horde Breaker
en.Your tenacity can wear down the most pot: Your tenacity can wear down the toughest targets. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage if it's below its hit point maximum. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.
en.Hunter's Prey: Giant Killer: Hunter's Prey: Bring Down the Big Ones
en.When a Large or larger creature within 5: When a Large or larger creature within 5 feet of you hits or misses you with an attack, you can use your reaction to attack that creature immediately after its attack, provided that you can see the creature.
en.Once on each of your turns when you make: Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within range of your weapon.
en.Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your: Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action and expend one Hunter technique slot to stop, listen, and read the land around you: the wind, the birds going quiet, tracks, smells, broken branches. For 1 minute per level of the technique slot you expend, you can tell whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or within up to 6 miles if you are in your favored terrain): mutants, zealots, apex predators, firebugs, drifters, cultists, and the dead. This feature doesn't reveal the creatures' location or number.
en.At 7th level, you gain one of the follow:
At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Escape the Horde
Multiattack Defense
Steel Will
en.Opportunity attacks against you are made: You know how to slip between grabbing hands. Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.
en.When a creature hits you with an attack,: When a creature hits you with an attack, you read its rhythm: you gain a +4 bonus to AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.
en.You have advantage on saving throws agai: You've seen too much to panic now. You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
en.Starting at 8th level, moving through no:
Starting at 8th level, moving through natural difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through brush, brambles, and undergrowth without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against snares, netting, wire, and rigged vegetation set up to impede movement, such as a tangle trap laid across a trail.
en.Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1:
Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other materials at hand with which to create your camouflage.
Once you are camouflaged in this way, you can try to hide by pressing yourself up against a solid surface, such as a tree or wall, that is at least as tall and wide as you are. You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions. Once you move or take an action or a reaction, you must camouflage yourself again to gain this benefit.
en.At 11th level, you gain one of the follo:
At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Volley
Whirlwind Attack
en.You can use your action to make a ranged: You can use your action to make a ranged attack against any number of creatures within 10 feet of a point you can see within your weapon's range. You must have ammunition for each target, as normal, and you make a separate attack roll for each target.
en.You can use your action to make a melee: You can use your action to make a melee attack against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target.
en.Starting at 14th level, you can use the: Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by ordinary means, unless you choose to leave a trail.
en.At 15th level, you gain one of the follo:
At 15th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Evasion
Stand Against the Tide
Uncanny Dodge
en.When you are subjected to an effect, suc: When you are subjected to an effect, such as a propane tank going up or a shotgun blast, that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
en.Superior Hunter's Defense: Stand Against: Superior Hunter's Defense: Stand Against the Tide
en.When a hostile creature misses you with: When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to sidestep and steer the blow, forcing that creature to repeat the same attack against another creature (other than itself) of your choice.
en.When an attacker that you can see hits y: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.
en.At 18th level, you gain preternatural se:
At 18th level, years in the dark have honed your hearing and smell until they help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.
You are also aware of the location of any unseen creature within 30 feet of you (in darkness, smoke, or out of sight), provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.
en.At 20th level, you become an unparallele: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your chosen prey. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.
en.Over 1 hour of shared hunting and a bloo: Over 1 hour of shared hunting, food, and patient handling, you bond with an animal of one of these kinds: wolfdog, mountain cat, mastiff, feral hog, badger, hawk, coyote, or rattlesnake (use the closest SRD stat block, CR 1/4 or lower). Add your proficiency bonus to its AC, attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws. Its hit point maximum is 4 × your Hunter level or its normal maximum, whichever is higher. It shares your initiative and acts right after you. It moves on its own and, without orders, takes the Dodge action. As a bonus action, you can command it to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, Help, or Hide action on its turn. If you are incapacitated, it acts on its own to protect you. If it dies, you can bond with a new animal by repeating the process; or, within 1 hour of its death, you can spend 1 minute and expend a technique slot on emergency care (clearing the airway, chest compressions, packing the wound) to bring it back with 1 hit point.
en.You and your companion share a language: You and your companion share a language of glances, hand signs, and whistles. While it is within 100 feet of you and can see or hear you, it understands simple commands. As an action, you can focus entirely on your companion's reactions (its ears, its hackles, its nose) and use its senses as your own until the start of your next turn (you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings while doing so). Your companion also adds your proficiency bonus to Wisdom (Perception) and Dexterity (Stealth) checks it makes.
en.Your companion's attacks count as magica: Your companion's attacks punch through resistance and immunity that stop ordinary attacks. In addition, when a creature within 5 feet of your companion makes an attack against you, your companion can use its reaction to make one melee attack against that creature, even if you didn't command it to attack this round.
en.When you command your companion to take: When you command your companion to take the Attack action, it can make two attacks instead of one, or make one attack and then take the Dash or Disengage action as part of the same action. In addition, once per turn when both you and your companion hit the same creature during the same round, that creature takes an extra 1d8 damage of the companion's attack type.
en.Your bond lets you share each other's wo: You look out for each other, whatever it costs. When you or your companion takes damage while the two of you are within 30 feet of each other, the other can use its reaction to throw itself into the way and take half of that damage instead (it can't be reduced further). In addition, your companion has advantage on saving throws against techniques, and while it is within 30 feet of you, neither of you can be talked into things or frightened by a creature the other can see.
en.You hone your skills in the larcenous ar: You hone your skills in the art of getting in and getting out. Burglars, shoplifters, pickpockets, and car thieves typically follow this racket, but so do people who prefer to think of themselves as salvage experts, urban explorers, repo agents, and private investigators. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you learn skills useful for working through abandoned buildings, reading unfamiliar codes and labels, and getting gear to work that was never meant for you.
en.Cutthroats are paid to end things quickl: Muggers end things quickly. They plan the approach, choose the moment, and strike before the target knows a fight has begun, then vanish before anyone can answer. Poison, patience, and a steady hand are their whole philosophy.
en.Hexthieves picked up their magic the way: Con artists picked up their tricks the way they pick up everything else: by taking them. A few stolen routines and smooth lines, learned by heart and never written down, let them fool eyes, work on minds, and walk out with the prize while everyone argues about what they saw.
en.At 1st level, choose two of your skill p:
At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with lockpicks. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with lockpicks) to gain this benefit
en.Beginning at 1st level, you know how to:
Beginning at 1st level, you know how to hit where it hurts and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.
You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.
The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this profession, as shown in the Cheap Shot column of the Locksmith table.
en.During your rogue training you learned t:
During your years on the street you learned street slang, a private mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows the slang understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.
In addition, you understand a set of tags, chalk marks, and graffiti used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or claimed by a crew, whether supplies are stashed nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a safe house for someone on the run.
en.Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinki: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.
en.At 3rd level, you choose an archetype th: At 3rd level, you choose a racket that you follow in the exercise of your Locksmith abilities, such as Burglar. Additional rackets are available in the original source material. Your racket choice grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.
en.Starting at 3rd level, you can use the b: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your lockpicks to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.
en.When you choose this archetype at 3rd le:
When you choose this racket at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.
en.When you reach 4th level, and again at 8: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
en.Starting at 5th level, when an attacker: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.
en.Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly d: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a gas tank going up or a grenade going off. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
en.Starting at 9th level, you have advantag: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
en.By 11th level, you have refined your cho: By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
en.By 13th level, you have learned enough a: By 13th level, you have figured out enough about how gear works (overrides, bypasses, factory defaults, the trick every manual leaves out) that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all profession, origin, and level requirements on the use of special items.
en.Starting at 14th level, if you are able: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or unseen creature within 10 feet of you.
en.By 15th level, you have acquired greater: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.
en.When you reach 17th level, you have beco: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.
en.Beginning at 18th level, you are so evas: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.
en.At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack:
At 20th level, you have an uncanny way of coming through when it counts. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
en.You are deadliest in the first moments o: You are deadliest in the first moments of a fight. In the first round of combat, any creature that has not yet acted is caught flat-footed by you: your attack rolls against it are made with advantage. In addition, the first time on each of your turns during that first round that you hit a creature with Cheap Shot, add extra damage equal to your Locksmith level to that attack.
en.You gain proficiency with the poisoner's: You gain proficiency with the poisoner's kit and with your choice of the forgery kit or the herbalism kit. In addition, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to blend into a crowd, and on Charisma (Deception) checks made to talk your way past a guard or checkpoint while carrying forged papers or a plausible errand.
en.During a short or long rest, using a poi: During a short or long rest, using a poisoner's kit, you can cook up a dose of homemade poison from whatever is under the sink (no cost). As a bonus action you can coat one weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition; the coating lasts 1 minute or until it hits. A creature hit by a coated weapon must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). On a failure it takes an extra 3d6 poison damage and is poisoned until the end of its next turn; on a success it takes half the damage and isn't poisoned. You can prepare a number of doses equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining uses on a long rest; unused doses spoil after 24 hours.
en.When you reduce a creature to 0 hit poin: When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points on your turn, you can immediately move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks. If you end that movement lightly obscured or behind at least half cover, you can also take the Hide action as part of the same move, without using an action or bonus action. In addition, you can't be tracked by ordinary means unless you choose to leave a trail.
en.When you hit a creature with Sneak Attac: When you hit a creature with Cheap Shot and it hasn't yet taken a turn in the current combat, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). On a failure, roll your Cheap Shot dice a second time and add the result to the damage. Once per short or long rest, you can use this feature against a creature that has already acted, provided it is below half its hit point maximum when you hit it.
en.You gain innate illusion and enchantment: You've learned the patter, props, and misdirection of the trade. Intelligence is your technique ability for techniques used with Con Artist features: your technique save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier and your technique attack modifier is your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. You don't use technique slots; these techniques are used at their lowest level and need no supplies unless they call for a costly item. You know Decoy and one other knack of your choice from: Flashlight Games, Long Reach, Pass the Word, Pocket Tricks, Trash Talk. You can use them at will.
en.Choose three of the following 1st-level: Choose three of the following 1st-level techniques: Sweet Talk, Flash in the Eyes, Quick Disguise, Crack Them Up, Staged Scene, Spiked Drink. You can use any of them at 1st level without a technique slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest. Whenever you gain a Locksmith level, you can replace one chosen technique with another from the list.
en.You can cast your Hexthief spells withou: You can use your Con Artist techniques without saying a word or making an obvious gesture unless the technique deals damage, so long as you have a hand free or are holding a set of lockpicks. A creature can notice what you're doing only with a successful Wisdom (Perception) check contested by your Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. In addition, once per turn when you use a Con Artist technique, you can make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check as part of the same action to plant or lift a small object on a creature within 5 feet of you, contested by its Wisdom (Perception).
en.You learn two of the following 2nd-level: You learn two of the following 2nd-level techniques: Hard to Pin, Freeze!, Nobody Saw Me, Body Doubles, Slip Away, Plant an Idea. You can use either of them at 2nd level without a technique slot, twice in total, regaining both uses when you finish a long rest (you can also expend two Pocket Cons uses to use one). In addition, once per turn when you deal Cheap Shot damage to a creature, you can forgo two of your Cheap Shot dice to force it to make a Wisdom save against your technique save DC or be charmed by you (rattled, hanging on your every word) until the end of its next turn.
en.When a creature fails a saving throw aga: When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Con Artist techniques, or interacts with one of your fakes or setups without seeing through it, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of your next turn, and you can deal Cheap Shot to it without needing an ally nearby. You also learn one of Big Production or Light Show and can use it at 3rd level without a technique slot once per long rest.
en.Once per long rest, you can cast greater: Once per long rest, you can use Ghost in the Crowd on yourself without a technique slot: for 1 minute nobody registers you, as long as you keep to shadows, crowds, and blind spots (the DM adjudicates where that's possible). For this use the technique doesn't require concentration. While it lasts, you can still deal Cheap Shot to any creature that can't see you, even without advantage from another source or an ally nearby, and taking the Hide action costs you no action.
en.When a creature you can see succeeds on: When a creature you can see succeeds on a saving throw against one of your Con Artist techniques, you can use your reaction to double down on the lie and force it to reroll the save, using the new result. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.
en.Your innate magic comes from draconic ma: Your edge was forged in collisions: football, rugby, hockey, wrestling, the cage. Years of hitting and getting hit taught your body to shrug off what drops other people, and somewhere along the way you picked up a signature dirty trick that has kept you alive since the dead started walking. Some contact athletes come from families who played the same game for generations; most just found it on their own. Any given athlete could be the first in their family to find out how much punishment a body can take, and how much it can dish out.
en.Somewhere in your ancestry, a forebear d: Somewhere along the way you started chasing the edge: rooftop runs, big drops, downhill lines nobody sane would ride. That appetite for risk never left, and now it runs in your veins. Your techniques come out a little crooked, often in your favor and sometimes spectacularly not, and luck itself seems to lean toward you when you push it hard enough.
en.An event in your past, or in the life of: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or coach, left an indelible mark on you: years of drills, a body that simply works differently, a hunger to win that never switched off. That raw physical talent, whatever its origin, fuels your techniques.
en.Choose a sorcerous origin, which describ:
Choose a sport, which describes where your physical edge comes from, such as Contact Sports.
Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.
en.At 1st level, you choose one type of dra:
At 1st level, you choose a signature style: the dirty trick you bring to every fight. The damage type associated with each style is used by features you gain later.
You know the playbook, the trash talk and the locker-room code of your sport. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with hardened fighters (bouncers, brawlers, gang muscle and other athletes), your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
en.Dragon Ancestor: Black - Acid Damage: Signature Style: Drain Cleaner - Acid Damage
en.Dragon Ancestor: Blue - Lightning Damage: Signature Style: Stun Baton - Lightning Damage
en.Dragon Ancestor: Brass - Fire Damage: Signature Style: Lighter Fluid - Fire Damage
en.Dragon Ancestor: Bronze - Lightning Dama: Signature Style: Car Battery - Lightning Damage
en.Dragon Ancestor: Copper - Acid Damage: Signature Style: Battery Acid - Acid Damage
en.Dragon Ancestor: Gold - Fire Damage: Signature Style: Gas Can - Fire Damage
en.Dragon Ancestor: Silver - Cold Damage: Signature Style: Fire Extinguisher - Cold Damage
en.Dragon Ancestor: White - Cold Damage: Signature Style: Ice Bath - Cold Damage
en.As magic flows through your body, it cau:
As your training keeps paying off, your body hardens like a lifetime of contact made it. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.
Additionally, scar tissue, calluses and dense muscle let you roll with hits that would floor anyone else. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
en.At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellsp:
At 2nd level, you learn to dig into reserves most people never reach. Those reserves are represented by grit points, which let you push your techniques past their normal limits.
Grit Points
You have 2 grit points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Grit Points column of the Athlete table. You can never have more grit points than shown on the table for your level. You regain all spent grit points when you finish a long rest.
en.Flexible Casting: Creating Spell Slots: Dig Deep: Grit into Technique Slots
en.You can transform unexpended sorcery poi:
You can turn unexpended grit points into one technique slot as a bonus action on your turn. The Creating Technique Slots table shows the cost of creating a technique slot of a given level. You can create technique slots no higher in level than 5th. 
Any technique slot you create with this feature is gone when you finish a long rest.
en.Flexible Casting: Converting Spell Slot: Dig Deep: Technique Slot into Grit
en.As a bonus action on your turn, you can: As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend one technique slot and gain a number of grit points equal to the slot's level.
en.At 3rd level, you gain the ability to tw:
At 3rd level, you learn to push your techniques past what your body should allow. You gain two of the following Pushing Limits options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.
You can use only one Pushing Limits option on a technique when you use it, unless otherwise noted.
en.When you cast a spell that forces other: When you use a technique that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can spare some of those creatures its full force. To do so, you spend 1 grit point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the technique.
en.When you cast a spell that has a range o:
When you use a technique that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 grit point to double the range of the technique.
When you use a technique that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 grit point to make the range of the technique 30 feet.
en.When you roll damage for a spell, you ca:
When you roll damage for a technique, you can spend 1 grit point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). You must use the new rolls.
You can use Full Power even if you have already used a different Pushing Limits option while using the technique.
en.When you cast a spell that has a duratio: When you use a technique that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 grit point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.
en.When you cast a spell that forces a crea: When you use a technique that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 3 grit points to catch one target of the technique off balance, giving it disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the technique.
en.When you cast a spell that has a casting: When you use a technique that takes 1 action to use, you can spend 2 grit points to use it as 1 bonus action instead this time.
en.When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 s: When you use a technique, you can spend 1 grit point to use it without any telltale windup or shout: it needs no somatic or verbal components.
en.When you cast a spell that targets only:
When you use a technique that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of grit points equal to the technique's level to target a second creature in range with the same technique (1 grit point if the technique is a knack).
To be eligible, a technique must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the technique's current level. For example, a spray of thrown nails or a flurry of hurled bottles isn't eligible, but a single hurled brick is.
en.Starting at 6th level, when you cast a s: Starting at 6th level, when you use a technique that deals damage of the type tied to your signature style, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that technique. At the same time, you can spend 1 grit point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour: you've been burned, shocked or frozen by your own tricks often enough to take it.
en.At 14th level, you gain the ability to s:
At 14th level, you can switch into an all-out free-running stride that turns walls, railings, cars and rooftops into open ground, gaining a climbing speed equal to your current speed. While in this stride you can leap gaps, wall-run and vault up onto any ledge or surface you could reach with that much movement, and you land rolls from such heights without taking falling damage; the DM decides which routes are runnable. You can enter this stride as a bonus action on your turn. It lasts until you end it as a bonus action on your turn.
You can't run like this while wearing armor unless the armor is made to allow it, and clothing not made for it might be torn apart when you do.
en.Beginning at 18th level, you can channel: Beginning at 18th level, you can put on the presence that made rivals fold before the whistle, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 grit points to draw on this presence and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were using a concentration technique), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.
en.At 20th level, you regain 4 expended sor: At 20th level, you regain 4 expended grit points whenever you finish a short rest.
en.Starting when you choose this origin at:
Starting when you choose this sport at 1st level, you ride too close to the edge. Immediately after you use an Athlete technique of 1st level or higher, roll a d20. On a 1, things go sideways: roll a d20 again and apply the matching effect from the Sideways table below. If you applied any Pushing Limits option to the technique, things go sideways on a 1 or 2 instead. Effects that call for a save use your technique save DC, and a sideways result never interrupts the technique that caused it (it resolves after the technique's effects).
Sideways table (d20):
1 — Big Bang. Something you hit or kick (a propane tank, a tire, a transformer box) bursts with a deafening crack. You and each other creature within 10 feet of you take 2d6 thunder damage (no saving throw).
2 — Bail. You lose your line and go flying 30 feet to an unoccupied space in a random direction, clearing anything in between (roll a d8: 1 north, 2 northeast, 3 east, and so on clockwise). If that space is occupied or solid, you land in the nearest unoccupied space toward it.
3 — Road Rash. Scrapes and bruises bloom blue-black across your skin until you finish a long rest. This has no other effect.
4 — Lit Up. A glow stick on your gear snaps or your headlamp jams on. For 1 minute, you shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet, and you can't benefit from being hidden or invisible.
5 — Gone. You drop out of sight in a blur of motion and are invisible until the start of your next turn, or until you make an attack roll or use a technique.
6 — Dust Cloud. You kick up a choking cloud of dust, chalk and plaster that fills a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on you for 1 minute. The area is lightly obscured; a strong wind disperses it.
7 — Runner's High. You regain 1d4 grit points (up to your maximum). If you don't have Deep Reserves, you instead gain 1d4 + your Charisma modifier temporary hit points.
8 — Gassed. You lose 1d4 grit points (minimum 0). If you have none, you instead take 1d4 force damage from pure strain that can't be reduced.
9 — Big Air. You launch 10 feet into the air off a wall or railing and stay up there, wall-running and bouncing between surfaces, until the end of your next turn (you can move as if you had a 30-foot flying speed), then drop and roll out without taking falling damage.
10 — Crowd Goes Wild. The stunt is so outrageous it jolts everyone nearby. You and each creature within 30 feet of you regain 1d8 hit points.
11 — Bad Feeling. Your nerve cracks. You are frightened of the creature closest to you (DM's choice among ties) until the end of your next turn.
12 — Second Gear. Your walking speed increases by 20 feet for 1 minute.
13 — Rattled Them. The first creature that makes a saving throw against one of your techniques before the end of your next turn does so with disadvantage. If the technique that triggered this result forced a save, this applies to the next technique instead.
14 — Earworm. A song gets stuck in your head. For 1 minute, you can speak only in rhyming couplets. This doesn't stop you from using techniques with verbal components.
15 — Juke. You sell a fake so hard your opponents can't track you. Until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have disadvantage.
16 — Stuck. Your foot jams in a grate, a crack or a tangle of cable. Your speed becomes 0 until the end of your next turn.
17 — Flare Belt. A road flare tucked in your gear sputters alight. For 1 minute, any creature that hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet of you takes 1d6 fire damage.
18 — Numb. The pain just stops registering. You gain 2d10 temporary hit points.
19 — Switcheroo. Choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You dive, roll or shove past it and the two of you trade places. An unwilling creature can make a Charisma saving throw against your technique save DC to resist; if it succeeds, nothing happens.
20 — Clutch. You regain your lowest-level expended technique slot of 5th level or lower. If you have no expended slots, you instead gain 1 grit point (if you have Deep Reserves) or 2d10 temporary hit points.
en.Also at 1st level, you can tug on the th: Also at 1st level, you can push your luck. When you make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll a d4 after seeing the d20 result but before the DM says whether it succeeds, and either add the number to the roll or subtract it from the roll (your choice after seeing the d4). Each time you use this feature, the luck you borrowed comes due: until you finish a long rest, your Ragged Edge rolls go sideways on one additional number (a 1–2 instead of a 1, a 1–3 instead of a 1–2, and so on, to a maximum of 1–5).
en.Starting at 6th level, you can unravel a: Starting at 6th level, you can throw off another creature's timing with a shout, a feint or a kicked can at the worst moment. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 grit points to force it to reroll the d20 before the outcome is known. The creature must use the new roll, whether it is better or worse. After you use this feature, roll a d20: on a 1, things go sideways (roll on the Sideways table).
en.At 14th level, you learn to steer the ch: At 14th level, you learn to steer the chaos instead of merely surviving it. Whenever you roll on the Sideways table, you can add or subtract up to your Charisma modifier from that roll (minimum result 1, maximum 20) before applying the effect. In addition, when you use an Athlete technique of 1st level or higher, you can choose to make things go sideways without rolling to see whether they do; you can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest. A sideways result you cause this way can't produce the Clutch result (treat a final result of 20 as 19).
At 18th level, chaos bends to your will. When you roll damage for an Athlete technique, you can reroll any dice that show a 1, and you must use the new rolls (each die can be rerolled only once). In addition, when things go sideways, you can choose any entry from the Sideways table instead of rolling. Once you choose an entry this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
en.You have made a pact with a fiend from t: You owe the cartel, and the cartel never forgets a debt. Maybe they paid your lawyer, kept your family fed while you were inside, or opened your cell door the night the dead poured through the block. Their aims are ugly, even if you fight against them. What they want is control of everything worth having, and sooner or later that includes you. The world that made them is gone, but their reach is not: the people who can call in your debt include the boss who runs the river crossing, the lieutenants who move guns, fuel and medicine out of the old warehouses, the quartermaster sitting on the last pallets of antibiotics, and the hired killers who still collect for all of them.
en.Your patron rules a glittering court in: Your Connection owns the club: the neon, the back rooms, the generator that keeps the music going, the people who drink there and the ones who never left. Their moods swing with the playlist, and their favor is as dangerous as their scorn. You may be a bouncer, a dealer, collateral on someone else's debt, or simply an amusement they have not yet tired of. What they teach you is glamour, misdirection, and the authority to give an order that lesser people simply obey.
en.Your patron dwells in the cold spaces be: Your Connection is a voice on a phone that shouldn't still work: a burner that rings in the dead hours of the night, long after the towers went dark. You have never seen who is calling. They know things no one should know: where the dead are thickest tonight, names you never told anyone, what really happened before the outbreak. They speak to you in fragments: strings of numbers, coordinates, recordings of people who died before the first night. Whether they are guiding you, studying you, or merely using you is impossible to know.
en.At 1st level, you have struck a bargain: At 1st level, you owe someone dangerous: a Connection of your choice, such as the Cartel. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.
en.Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, the rush of the kill steels you: you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your Ex-Con level (minimum of 1).
en.Your arcane research and the magic besto: The people you owe, and the people who owe you, have taught you how to get things done that others can't. You call in Favors to pull off your techniques, and you get them back after a short rest.
en.In your study of occult lore, you have u:
Years in the yard taught you yard tricks: hard-won habits and hustles that never leave you.
At 2nd level, you gain two yard tricks of your choice. Your options are detailed at the end of the profession description. When you gain certain Ex-Con levels, you gain additional yard tricks of your choice, as shown in the Yard Tricks Known column of the Ex-Con table.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this profession, you can choose one of the yard tricks you know and replace it with another yard trick that you could learn at that level.
en.When you cast eldritch blast, add your C: When you use Shiv Flurry, you put your whole weight behind every blow: add your Charisma modifier to the damage it deals on a hit.
en.You can cast mage armor on yourself at w: You can pad yourself out at will with whatever is lying around, without spending a technique slot or supplies: magazines taped to your forearms, layered jackets, a strip of tire under your shirt. While you wear no other armor, the padding turns blows a little better than the best light armor.
en.You can cast speak with animals at will,: You spent years in the prison dog-training program. At will, without spending a technique slot, you can read and talk to animals: you understand what a beast is telling you through its posture and sounds, and you can get simple ideas across to it.
en.You gain proficiency in the Deception an: You gain proficiency in the Deception and Persuasion skills.
en.You can now inscribe magical rituals in:
You can now copy slow, careful techniques into your Library Book. Choose two 1st-level techniques from any profession's technique list that can be done the slow way (without spending a slot, taking ten extra minutes); the two needn't be from the same list. The techniques appear in the book and don't count against the number of techniques you know. With your Library Book in hand, you can use the chosen techniques the slow way. You can't use them any other way, unless you've learned them by some other means. You can also use an Ex-Con technique you know the slow way if it allows it.
On your runs, you can add other techniques that can be done the slow way to your Library Book. When you come across one (a manual, a field guide, someone willing to show you), you can add it to the book if the technique's level is equal to or less than half your Ex-Con level (rounded up) and if you can spare the time to copy it out. For each level of the technique, copying takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp worth of paper, ink and tape.
en.You can see normally in darkness, both m: Years of lights-out on the block trained your eyes. You can see normally in darkness of any kind, even a sealed basement without a crack of light, to a distance of 120 feet.
en.You can cast detect magic at will, witho: You've lived through a thousand cell shakedowns. At will, without spending a technique slot, you can sweep your surroundings with a guard's eye and sense what's hidden or rigged nearby: stashed weapons and contraband, false bottoms, tripwires and booby traps, tampered locks. You know something is there and roughly where; the DM tells you what you pick up.
en.When you cast eldritch blast, its range: When you use Shiv Flurry, you can hurl your blades with uncanny aim: its range is 300 feet.
You can read all writing. Years among people from everywhere taught you every alphabet, gang code, tattoo script and cipher ever scratched into a cell wall.
en.You can cast false life on yourself at w: At will, without spending a technique slot or supplies, you can grit your teeth and shut the pain out as a 1st-level technique, gaining a buffer of temporary hit points.
en.You can use your action to touch a willi: You can use your action to clip a radio earpiece on a willing humanoid and tune in to them completely: they murmur everything they notice and the open line carries the rest, so you perceive through their senses until the end of your next turn. As long as you stay within radio range of each other, you can use your action on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses that creature has, and you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings, eyes shut and every scrap of attention on the line.
en.You can cast disguise self at will, with: At will, without spending a technique slot, you can change your look in moments: a borrowed jacket, a cap pulled low, a shaved head or a smear of grime, a different walk and a different voice. Your disguise won't survive a hands-on inspection, but at a glance you could be anyone.
en.You can cast silent image at will, witho: At will, without spending a technique slot or supplies, you can rig a convincing decoy from whatever is at hand: a coat on a broom in a window, a shadow thrown across a wall, a flashlight bobbing down a stairwell. It's silent and purely visual, and anyone who takes a close look sees it for what it is.
en.When you hit a creature with eldritch bl: When you hit a creature with Shiv Flurry, you can drive it back with the force of your assault: push the creature up to 10 feet away from you in a straight line.
en.You can cast bane once using a warlock s: Once, by spending one of your Ex-Con technique slots, you can rattle a few enemies with a cold stare and a well-placed threat, so that for a while their attacks and saving throws keep coming up short. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
en.You can communicate telepathically with:
You can stay in constant contact with your Lookout through a cheap two-way radio, whistles and hand signals, and perceive what your Lookout sees and hears as long as you are within radio range of each other.
Additionally, while perceiving through your Lookout's senses, you can also speak through your Lookout in your own voice, over the radio clipped to them, even if your Lookout is normally incapable of speech.
en.You can cast slow once using a warlock s: Once, by spending one of your Ex-Con technique slots, you can throw a group of enemies off their rhythm with feints, false orders and a barrage of noise, until they move and react sluggishly, as if wading through mud. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
en.Eldritch Invocation: One with Shadows: Yard Trick: Melt Into the Dark
en.When you are in an area of dim light or: When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to go perfectly still in a corner or against a wall, the way you learned to vanish between head counts. You are invisible until you move or take an action or a reaction.
en.You can cast bestow curse once using a w: Once, by spending one of your Ex-Con technique slots, you can mark one creature you can touch with a threat it can't shake (a whisper in its ear, a cut, a promise), leaving it off its game in a way you choose with the DM: fumbling one kind of check or saving throw, struggling to land blows on you, freezing up instead of acting, or bleeding extra from your attacks. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
